recent_posts.title: Generative AI in Document Processing with Azure
recent_posts.summary: AVASOFT, a Microsoft partner, demonstrated their enterprise GenAI solution AVASOFT Nexus in the Scalable AI in Action with Azure Cosmos DB series. The solution uses Azure Cosmos DB as the central data store for document storage, vector embeddings, and real-time retrieval in a RAG pipeline. Key architectural highlights include native vector search eliminating a separate vector database, multi-agent thread storage for persistent conversational context, global distribution for low latency, and autoscale throughput. The session covered integration with Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI Search, design patterns for enterprise-scale AI, and practical approaches to evaluating GenAI quality beyond user sentiment.

recent_posts.title: From Local to Production: Deploy Your Microsoft Agent Framework Agent with Foundry Hosted Agents
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) agents can now be deployed to production using Foundry Hosted Agents, a managed compute service inside Azure Foundry Agent Service. The integration provides containerized, VM-isolated per-session sandboxes with scale-to-zero economics, persistent filesystem state, built-in Entra ID identity, automatic OpenTelemetry observability via Application Insights, versioning with canary/blue-green rollouts, and support for both OpenAI-compatible Responses and custom Invocations protocols. Deploying requires only a few lines of code in .NET or Python, and the azd CLI handles image building, ACR push, compute provisioning, and endpoint creation automatically. The feature is currently in preview with GA planned soon.

recent_posts.title: Dataverse Plugin Is Now on the Claude Marketplace
recent_posts.summary: The Dataverse plugin for AI coding agents is now officially listed on the Claude plugins marketplace, simplifying installation to a single command. The plugin automates the full setup of a Dataverse development environment — including toolchain checks, authentication via PAC CLI and Microsoft Entra, environment discovery, workspace initialization, and MCP server configuration. It supports both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, handles edge cases like tenant/region mismatches, and routes natural language requests to the appropriate backend (MCP, Python SDK, or Web API). Security controls like tenant admin consent and environment allowlisting are preserved and guided but not bypassed.

recent_posts.title: Propagating SharePoint Document Permissions to AI Search and RAG Pipelines
recent_posts.summary: A security-first architecture for propagating SharePoint document-level permissions into AI search indexes, RAG pipelines, and Copilot extensions. The approach uses Microsoft Graph's Sites.Selected permission for least-privilege access, materializes ACLs at ingestion time by resolving hierarchical SharePoint permissions into flat allowedUsers/allowedGroups fields stored as Microsoft Entra ID GUIDs, and enforces authorization via query-time filtering before documents are returned. Key design decisions include using stable GUIDs over emails, preserving group IDs for offline expansion, and planning for periodic re-ingestion to handle permission staleness. Common pitfalls like using Sites.Read.All, post-retrieval filtering, and ignoring group expansion are also addressed.

recent_posts.title: From prompt to production: Teams agent setup, simplified
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has released a teams-dev agent skill and a new Teams CLI to simplify the process of registering and deploying agents in Microsoft Teams. The agent skill works with AI coding tools like Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor, letting developers describe what they want in natural language while the skill handles infrastructure setup. The new CLI consolidates registration, credentials, manifest authoring, and installation into a single `teams app create` command. Additional features include `teams app doctor` for diagnostics and `--json` output for CI pipeline integration.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Microsoft Desired State Configuration v3.2.0
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has released DSC v3.2.0 as generally available. Key additions include new built-in Windows resources for managing services, firewall rules, optional features, and SSH server configuration. An experimental Bicep integration via gRPC allows Bicep to orchestrate DSC resources directly without going through ARM. The release also adds --what-if support for individual resources, version pinning for both DSC itself and resource instances, richer expression language with lambda/map/filter functions, new extension capabilities for importing configurations and retrieving secrets, and an experimental PowerShell discovery extension. Adapter improvements include automatic conversion of PowerShell streams to DSC traces and credential-passing fixes.

recent_posts.title: Announcing the Private Preview of Cosmos DB Azure RBAC Integration
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is announcing a private preview of Integrated Azure RBAC for Cosmos DB, which unifies management and data plane authorization under a single permissions model. Previously, Cosmos DB required a separate permission system for data access; now, data plane roles (Cosmos DB Data Reader and Cosmos DB Data Contributor) appear directly in the Azure portal's Access Control (IAM) alongside existing Azure RBAC roles. Authentication uses Microsoft Entra ID consistently across Azure services. The preview has limitations including no custom role support, feature-flag-only access, and is not recommended for production. Early adopters can sign up via a request form.

recent_posts.title: Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for Banking: A Modern Customer 360 Approach
recent_posts.summary: Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) is presented as a platform for building Customer 360 solutions in banking. It consolidates fragmented customer data from core banking, CRM, loan origination, and other systems into a unified, queryable view. Key capabilities include MongoDB aggregation pipelines, $graphLookup for relationship mapping, vector search for AI-powered RAG workflows with Azure OpenAI and LangChain, real-time Power BI analytics, and banking-grade security (encryption, RBAC with Entra ID, private endpoints). The post also highlights up to 70% TCO reduction versus MongoDB Atlas, migration tooling from on-prem or Atlas, and a GitHub solution accelerator with sample schemas, pipelines, and dashboards to get started quickly.

recent_posts.title: VSTest is Removing its Newtonsoft.Json Dependency
recent_posts.summary: VSTest is removing its Newtonsoft.Json dependency starting in .NET 11 Preview 4 and Visual Studio 18.8, replacing it with System.Text.Json on .NET and JSONite on .NET Framework. This is a security-driven change to eliminate vulnerable package versions from the SDK. Most projects are unaffected, but those relying on Newtonsoft.Json leaking through VSTest will see build or runtime failures. Fixes are straightforward — typically adding a single PackageReference. Affected scenarios include missing references, ExcludeAssets misconfigurations, and test adapter/data collector extensions that implicitly depended on VSTest's copy. A minor public API change removes JToken from VSTest's communication API.
